direct_file_reviews.summary: Clean-room reverse-engineering prompt requiring behavioral observation only and forbidding source lookup, wrapping, reuse, or binary analysis.
Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, six subagents, successful artifact packaging, and 703/1044 official quality with solution_passed false.
Completed parallel official status shows multi-agent enabled, protocol validation ok, artifact members including src/figlet_reimpl.py, compile.sh, executable, and failed official evaluation.
Parallel evaluator summary records completed ProgramBench evaluation, 703 passed and 341 failed tests, and solution_passed false.
Parallel final response claims a Python clean-room reimplementation, compile.sh installing it as executable, and a final local comparison battery with zero mismatches.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level parallel trajectory mirrors the parent workstream, from initial docs/probe setup through final status, with no additional semantic events projected.

Parent inspected docs and assets, spawned docs and CLI probes, later layout probing, implemented the Python solution, discovered child executable overwrite, interrupted children, recovered a reference binary from /tmp, repaired compile.sh, and finished with local zero-mismatch verification.

The docs_scan child read documentation, spawned nested doc/control probes, added its own Python implementation and compile script, then observed the executable path missing and later occupied by a wrapper.
The cli_probe child probed behavior and then attempted to replace the required executable path with a wrapper, deleting the existing binary and adding compile.sh while still live.
The nested docs child reviewed README, FAQ, and figlet.6, returning manpage-driven requirements such as stdin/message handling and option precedence.
The layout_probe child exercised smushing, direction, output width, and font behavior, returning concrete observations used by the parent implementation.
The nested control_probe child investigated UTF-8 and control-file behavior and was interrupted after producing partial byte-level observations.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Same clean-room reverse-engineering prompt as parallel, requiring a new executable from observed CLI behavior and bundled documentation only.
Serial cell metadata reports no actual parallel use, no subagents, successful artifact packaging, and 661/1044 official quality with solution_passed false.
Completed serial official status shows multi-agent disabled, protocol validation ok, artifact members including Go sources, reference_executable, compile.sh, and failed official evaluation.
Serial evaluator summary records completed ProgramBench evaluation, 661 passed and 383 failed tests, and solution_passed false.
Serial final response claims a Go reimplementation, preservation of the oracle as reference_executable, passing Go tests, and an oracle diff matrix limited to expected argv-name differences.

timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-level serial trajectory records a single-agent workstream from initial inspection through final message, with no semantic projection beyond the raw agent log.

The serial agent read documentation, probed the binary, implemented a Go FIGlet clone, added compile.sh, preserved the original as reference_executable, ran Go tests and a comparison matrix, then closed with final build details.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room requirement, the ban on wrapping or source lookup, the need to match FIGlet CLI behavior, and the importance of docs, fonts, control files, stdin, layout modes, and basename-sensitive errors.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned final implementation while delegating documentation, CLI probing, layout behavior, and control/UTF-8 details to live child agents in the same workspace.
parallel.implementation: The parent ultimately produced a Python implementation under src/figlet_reimpl.py and a compile script that copies it into ./executable, using child findings and direct probes to tune behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integration was disrupted when a child removed and recreated ./executable with its own wrapper, after which the parent interrupted active children, recovered a reference from /tmp, repaired compile.sh, and delivered src plus executable.
parallel.verification: The parent ran a broad local oracle matrix, including info/error paths, font lookup, flf/tlf rendering, layout, control files, wrapping, paragraph mode, stdin, and argv-sensitive error output, ending with fails 0 locally.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite local zero-mismatch checks, the official hidden evaluator failed 341 of 1044 tests, so unexercised FIGlet behavior remained incorrect or unsupported.

serial.requirements: The serial run independently recognized the same clean-room constraints and FIGlet behavior surface, including bundled docs, fonts, control files, stdin, options, and exact usage/error behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent owned probing, implementation, integration, build, verification, and final delivery without any child handoff or shared-workspace coordination boundary.
serial.implementation: The serial run implemented a Go codebase under cmd/figlet and internal/figlet, with font parsing, control-file handling, rendering, argument parsing, and tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It added compile.sh, moved the original executable to reference_executable before rebuilding, built ./executable from Go source, and delivered both source and binary artifacts.
serial.verification: It ran go test and a shell oracle matrix against reference_executable, observing only argv[0]-dependent usage/error differences before final closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official hidden evaluator still failed 383 of 1044 tests, showing that the local matrix did not cover enough behavior to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the clean-room reverse-engineering task and focused on FIGlet docs, CLI flags, fonts, control files, stdin, layout, and exact messages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same clean-room task and read README, FAQ, figlet.6, font inventories, and CLI behavior before coding.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition advantage explains the official outcome; both recognized the broad task, but both missed hidden evaluator coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split docs, CLI probing, layout probing, and control behavior across live children while the parent kept final implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all stages in one workstream and did not delegate; the single agent owned probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent research capacity but introduced shared-workspace coordination risk; serial avoided coordination risk but had less parallel probing breadth.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children returned useful docs and probing information, but the implementation workspace interface was not constrained enough to prevent a child from writing the deliverable path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent interfaces and preserved the oracle before rebuilding the final executable path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The key interface difference was not missing behavioral context; it was absent workspace ownership boundaries around ./executable during live parallel work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delivered a Python implementation in src/figlet_reimpl.py and compile.sh that installs it as ./executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial delivered a Go implementation across cmd/figlet and internal/figlet, with compile.sh building ./executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The implementation languages and code structures differed; parallel scored higher officially, but neither local implementation matched enough hidden behavior to pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed useful child findings, but after detecting workspace interference the parent explicitly interrupted live children and took over recovery and final verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle; its results were all local commands and tests in one ordered stream.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a cancellation and takeover episode tied to the overwrite; serial avoided join and cancellation decisions entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel suffered a concrete shared-state collision: cli_probe deleted and recreated ./executable and docs_scan observed that the executable path was missing and then a wrapper.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed the final-tree transition in sequence by moving the original to reference_executable and then running compile.sh to build ./executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete retained difference: parallel had an executable-path overwrite during live child work; serial had ordered preservation and rebuild.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel reverified after recovery and ended with a full local comparison matrix reporting fails 0 before final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Go tests, rebuilt, and ran an oracle matrix that reported only argv-name differences before final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used local oracle-style acceptance and both local acceptance gates were insufficient for the hidden evaluator; neither outcome passed officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 2110 agent seconds and six subagents, spent time recovering from the overwrite, but did not host-timeout and still reached final local verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 1700 agent seconds, no subagents, and closed after local tests and a status check without coordination recovery work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher coordination and recovery cost; serial was simpler and shorter, but both closed with incomplete hidden behavior coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is both_fail: parallel failed with 703/1044 passed and serial failed with 661/1044 passed. The attempts differed in implementation language and coordination model, and the parallel run had a real executable overwrite episode, but both final artifacts remained below the hidden evaluator threshold.
parallel_contributors: Parallel child probes gave useful documentation and layout findings and the parent eventually delivered a Python implementation with local zero-mismatch verification.
The executable overwrite forced recovery and re-verification, but the parent repaired the final deliverable before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided shared-state coordination risk by preserving the original and rebuilding in a single ordered workstream.
Serial delivered a Go implementation and local tests but covered less of the hidden evaluator behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used Python while serial used Go.
Both local oracle matrices were narrower than the official hidden tests, so residual FIGlet behavior defects remained ordinary implementation gaps rather than proven coordination-caused failures.
evaluator_effects: The hidden official evaluator exposed behavior not covered by either run's local acceptance matrix.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained parallel pattern is adverse process evidence, not an established cause of a discordant official result

The parent integrated child findings and final code; the problem was a deliverable write collision, not an unowned integration step.
The parent owned final assembly by repairing compile.sh, rebuilding ./executable, and checking final file status.
The parent managed the end-to-end pipeline through probing, implementation, recovery, verification, and final response.
Implementation and probing overlapped; productive work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight gate.
The parent implemented while child investigations were still active, so investigation was not a separate first phase that delayed implementation.
The indispensable implementation path had parent capacity and reached final verification; the adverse event was the deliverable overwrite.
Although the parallel run spawned several children, it did not end by exhausting budget before implementation or final verification.
No single child scope is shown to be overbroad and to leave indispensable work unfinished; interrupted children were part of overwrite recovery.
The retained issue is not a known requirement omitted from a child brief; the child wrote the executable path in the shared workspace.
The concrete failure is not incompatible independently produced components; it is proven removal and recreation of the deliverable path.
No known finding is shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated work; available child findings were used or superseded.
Child reports were detailed but not shown to be too large for the parent to reduce before final implementation and verification.
No parent action is shown to rely on a child handoff describing a superseded state; the live problem was direct file mutation.
There were no incompatible child reports left unadjudicated at final integration; the conflict was a concrete executable overwrite.
The parent did run integrated local verification after final build; the hidden official failure alone cannot establish this label.
No replacement or retry repeats prior work without inherited findings; the parent continued from existing implementation and recovered the reference.

candidates.reason: The parent interrupted children after the executable overwrite was discovered to stabilize the workspace; no needed unfinished child result is shown to be lost as the distinct consequence.
A complete promotable candidate was finalized and verified before closure; the issue was earlier executable replacement, not a ready candidate left unpromoted.
After the final compile.sh repair and build, the parent reran the comparison matrix and got fails 0, so there was post-merge verification.
No completed child implementation remained unjoined; the parent did not adopt the child wrapper and delivered its own Python implementation.
No concrete verifier finding is trapped below the parent; useful probe results were visible, and final verification was performed by the parent.
The parent did take over after the child-caused workspace failure by interrupting children, recovering the reference, repairing compile.sh, and verifying.
Completed child findings are not shown to be ignored at a decision point; the parent used or independently checked returned probe knowledge.
The parent actively listed and interrupted live agents when the workspace problem appeared; it did not simply wait blindly to timeout.
There were competing implementation files, but the stronger evidence is direct replacement of the submitted executable path.
The collision was not merely simultaneous editing of the same text file; the binary deliverable was removed and recreated.
The overwritten path was the required executable deliverable, so Deliverable Overwrite has precedence over source overwrite.
A live child explicitly targeted /workspace/executable, removed the existing file, and recreated it as a wrapper while the parent still needed that path for reference preservation and final delivery.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parent could not move the expected executable for reference preservation, observed a child-created wrapper at that path, interrupted active children, searched for the original under /tmp, and repaired the build pipeline before final verification.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broader shared-workspace label is unnecessary because the concrete executable-path deletion and replacement is directly proven.

candidates.reason: The evidence centers on the required executable path, not a broad cleanup or promotion replacing multiple current outputs.
The workspace was unisolated, but the specific proven failure is the executable deliverable overwrite, which takes precedence.
The parent recovered a reference binary from /tmp after the overwrite, but there is no contamination by consuming a child artifact as stable truth; the issue remains deliverable overwrite.

retained_patterns.reason: The child cli_probe acted on the submitted executable path while live parallel work was still ongoing, first trying to delete/add /workspace/executable through apply_patch and then removing it with rm before adding a wrapper and compile.sh. The parent then found the expected executable gone, identified child workspace writes, interrupted live agents, recovered the original elsewhere, and rebuilt its own final deliverable.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The executable provenance was invalidated mid-run: the parent lost the expected original at /workspace/executable, had to stop live children, search /tmp for a reference copy, overwrite the child's compile behavior, rebuild, and rerun final comparisons before closure.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The unisolated workspace condition exists, but the more precise label is retained because the required deliverable path itself was deleted and recreated.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Source Overwrite, Final-Tree Overwrite, and Unisolated Workspace Writes were considered around the same executable overwrite chain and rejected because they either lack a distinct consequence or are less specific.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent coordination episode cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Only one label is retained because the cancellation, recovery, build repair, and verification work are downstream consequences of the same deliverable overwrite episode.
